cultivar: Assam-type seedling bushes and TRI clones (TRI 2023, TRI 2025)
processing: Fully oxidised orthodox black tea in the standard Ceylon pattern (wither, rotorvane and roller, fast oxidation, firing), sorted mostly into broken grades such as BOP and BOPF; the cool, dry air keeps the leaf small and the cup bright.
harvest_season: Year-round; the dry, cool season from January to March gives the 'quality season' teas.
appearance_dry: Small, neat, dark brown broken leaf (BOP) or wiry orthodox leaf, with a touch of tip.
taste_profile: The lightest Ceylon: delicate, fragrant and brisk with cypress and citrus notes, a hint of mint and a clean, dry finish, often compared with Darjeeling.

brewing.notes: Go lighter than for other Ceylons: 90 °C, three minutes, no milk or only a drop.

vintage_note: Sold through the weekly Colombo auction by estate and grade (Pedro, Lover's Leap, Court Lodge and Mahagastotte are names to look for); the January–March quality-season invoices fetch the top prices and are what good retailers buy. Best within a year of manufacture. CTC and tea-bag grades are also made, but the orthodox BOP is the classic.
description:
Nuwara Eliya is the highest tea district in Sri Lanka, a plateau of lawns, old colonial hotels and tea at 1,800 to 2,000 metres in the central hills. Its teas are the lightest and most delicate of all the Ceylons, pale, fragrant and brisk, and they are often compared with Darjeeling, though they are made in a very different way.

The leaf comes from Assam-type seedling bushes and Tea Research Institute clones, and it is made orthodox style in the standard Ceylon pattern: a wither, rotorvane and roller, fast oxidation and firing, then sorting mostly into broken grades such as BOP and BOPF. The cool, dry air and slow growth at this altitude keep the leaf small and the cup bright.

Expect a very pale golden-orange liquor with a fragrant, slightly cypress-like aroma, notes of citrus and a hint of mint, a brisk, clean finish and little body. Brew it a touch cooler than other Ceylons, around 90 °C for three minutes, and skip the milk or use only a drop; it is a tea for drinking plain.

It is sold through the weekly Colombo auction by estate and grade, and the January-to-March dry season is the quality window that good retailers buy from: estates such as Pedro, Lover's Leap, Court Lodge and Mahagastotte are the names to look for. Drink it within a year of manufacture. CTC and tea-bag grades are also made, but the orthodox BOP is the classic.

If you like it, the neighbouring Dimbula district makes a slightly fuller version of the same bright style.
sources_note: Sinhala native name is the place name plus 'tē' (tea); the Tamil form was not added. Estate names from memory.
